subject: Computer Networking
title: Fiber Optic Cables
description: A micro-lesson that makes Fiber Optic Cables usable.

hook.text: Copper carries electricity. Fiber carries light. Light is faster, reaches farther, and ignores interference.

buildup.text: A fiber cable has a glass core thinner than a hair. Laser pulses encode data as flashes of light.

discovery.text: Single-mode fiber reaches 100+ km. Multi-mode uses multiple light paths but is limited to shorter runs.

twist.text: Fiber ignores electromagnetic interference. Run it next to power lines without issues.

climax.text: Modern fiber carries 100 Tbps per strand using wavelength-division multiplexing — many colors of light.

punchline.text: Fiber carries data as light. Nothing else matches its speed or range.

quiz.question: What advantage does fiber have over copper?
options: Immunity to electromagnetic interference and much longer range
Lower cost per meter of cable
Easier to splice and repair in the field

details.summary: Fiber optic cables transmit data as pulses of light through thin glass or plastic strands, achieving speeds of 100 Gbps and beyond over distances of many kilometers. Single-mode fiber supports longer distances while multi-mode fiber is used for shorter high-speed campus links.
details.whyItMatters: Fiber optics form the backbone of the internet and modern data centers. Understanding fiber types and capabilities is essential as networks shift from copper to optical connections.
takeaways: Fiber transmits data as light pulses through glass strands
Single-mode fiber supports distances over 100 kilometers
Fiber is immune to electromagnetic interference unlike copper

faq.question: What is the difference between single-mode and multi-mode fiber?
faq.answer: Single-mode fiber has a tiny 9-micron core that carries one light path, supporting distances over 100 kilometers. Multi-mode fiber has a larger 50 or 62.5-micron core carrying multiple light paths, limited to about 550 meters. Single-mode costs more for transceivers but less per meter of cable.

faq.question: Is fiber optic better than Ethernet cable?
faq.answer: Fiber supports much higher speeds over longer distances and is immune to electrical interference. Copper Ethernet is cheaper for short runs under 100 meters and does not require specialized tools for termination. Most networks use fiber for backbone links and copper for device connections.
